notable_absence.finding: The page's own port table gives IDENTICAL default numbers (8094 unencrypted / 18094 encrypted) for two DIFFERENT named ports: fts_http_port/fts_ssl_port (REST/HTTP, client-to-node) and fts_grpc_port/fts_grpc_ssl_port (gRPC, node-to-node, used for scatter-gather). A single port number cannot serve two different listener roles on the same node - this reads as a probable docs table error (the real fts_grpc_port is very likely a different number, distinct from the HTTP port), not a deliberate statement that FTS multiplexes both protocols on one port. Flagging for the docs-issues pass rather than resolving it myself, since extraction is quote-only and I cannot verify the correct number from this page alone.

cross_component_finding: This is the first page in the batch to state explicitly, in prose, that the gRPC port is 'used for [scatter-gather] operations between FTS nodes' and marks it Node-to-node only (not client-to-node, not XDCR) - a concrete transport detail neither fts-architecture.md nor fts-architecture-scatter-gather.md state (they describe the scatter/gather behavior but never name gRPC or a port number). server/8.0/search/search-index-architecture.json (round 22) does name gRPC as the scatter-gather transport but without a port number, so this page is the only one across both generations to pin down the actual port for the mechanism.
